note: Candidates reviewed for this update but not admitted, with the reason and the evidence that would reopen each.

entries.candidate: Goldfinch Technology Park proposed data-centre campus (Diode Ventures, a Black & Veatch company; about 575 acres in Wheatland County's Goldfinch Industrial ASP, Alberta; County file PL2025-005, Bylaws 2025-32 and 2025-34)
entries.reason: Identity and status are documented: Wheatland County's 7 July 2026 council highlights record first and second readings of Bylaw 2025-32 (Goldfinch Industrial ASP amendment 'to facilitate a new data processing facility development') and Bylaw 2025-34 (Agricultural General to Industrial General, 'supporting the development of a data processing facility'), with third readings set for 11 August 2026; the 11 August agenda (eSCRIBE HTML, local wheatland-council-agenda-2026-08-11.html) lists both third readings; Diode's project page (live capture of 22 October 2026; the Internet Archive CDX lists copies of 9 March and 22 August 2026, not fetched) says the ACP, ASP amendment and land-use bylaw amendment were 'approved in August 2026' and that development permits come next, with phases from 2029. That supports announced (redesignation is not consent for the data-centre development). No admissible locator was obtained: every eSCRIBE attachment (bylaw schedules, PL2025-005 map set, minutes) returns HTTP 403 to the research agent and was not pursued; the ASP attachment on the county site returns 404; Alberta Major Projects' point is marked 'not precise' and its description spans Range Roads 261-270 and Township Roads 220-222; Diode's April 2026 sheet shows only an unscaled site sketch (access moved from Highway 24 to Township Road 222).
entries.reopen_condition: An official parcel, legal land description with official geometry (e.g. Bylaw 2025-34 schedule plus an official ATS or parcel service), or the county's redesignation map for the Diode lands; admit as announced (third readings scheduled 11 August 2026, approval stated by Diode for August 2026) while within 90 days of the update, otherwise with a newer dated record such as a development permit.

entries.candidate: Microsoft Markham datacentre (Ontario) - with York Region site plan SP.23.M.0072 / Markham 23.116627.000.00.SPC 'Commerce Valley Drive East - Phase 1' (three-storey data centre, 33,243 m2 GFA, east of Leslie Street and south of Highway 7, PIN 030300019)
entries.reason: Microsoft's Markham Construction Update (published 5 August 2026, modified 6 August) says the first phase began on 8 May 2024 and the general contractor has prepared the site (demolition, fencing, grading), with building construction expected in late 2026 and a second building to be discussed in fall 2026; it gives no address. York Region's register (queried 22 October 2026) has exactly one Markham data-centre application, SP.23.M.0072 'Commerce Valley Drive East - Phase 1', received 14 April 2023, stage Review, seventh submission 31 July 2026, with an official application boundary (about 6 ha; centroid near 43.8447, -79.3740). The register names no owner or applicant, so the Microsoft link is circumstantial (demolished office site, Phase 1, Markham, site plan pending before late-2026 construction). Not admitted in this pass: the three-change cap was used by better-identified records, and naming the Markham record as Microsoft's would be unsupported.
entries.reopen_condition: Either (a) a City of Markham or York Region record naming Microsoft (or its project company) for SP.23.M.0072 / 23.116627, which would admit Microsoft Markham as site_preparation (5 August 2026) with the application-boundary centroid as campus locator; or (b) admit the register record alone as a new site 'Commerce Valley Drive East data centre - Phase 1' (announced, 31 July 2026; operator unknown) while it remains within 90 days (until 29 October 2026), or with a newer dated register event or approval.

entries.candidate: Bell AI Fabric Merritt, British Columbia facility (Bell data centre hosting the BUZZ HPC/Cohere cluster)
entries.reason: Bell's 18 June 2026 release (outside the window) says Bell will provide capacity from its Merritt facility 'purpose-built for advanced AI workloads'; BCE's 6 August 2026 Q2 release mentions only 'progress on the Merritt, B.C. expansion'; HIVE's 16 August 2026 release says the new cluster is 'expected to become operational later this year at the Bell AI Fabric facility in Merritt'. None states a dated physical status of the facility, and no address, parcel or municipal record was found (City of Merritt records not reached in this pass). Not in the Atlas.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated Bell, HIVE/BUZZ or City of Merritt record stating construction, completion or operation of the Merritt facility, with an official parcel or permit locator.
